title: Sections separating points and tangent vectors give a closed immersion
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $X$ a proper scheme over $k$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $k$-subspace. Suppose (0) for every closed point $x\in X$ some $s\in V$ does not vanish at $x$ (equivalently, $V$ generates $\mathcal L$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]); (1) for every pair of distinct closed points $x,y\in X$ some $s\in V$ vanishes at $x$ but not at $y$, and (2) for every closed point $x$ and every nonzero tangent vector $\theta\in T_{X/k,x}=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2,k)$ some $s\in V$ vanishes at $x$ and has nonzero first derivative along $\theta$. Then $V$ is finite-dimensional, and the morphism $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}:X\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ defined by a basis of $V$ is a closed immersion with $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. In particular, if $V=H^0(X,\mathcal L)$, the complete linear system is a closed immersion and $\mathcal L$ is very ample [def-sc-ample].

proof.text: Because $X$ is proper over $k$ and $\mathcal L$ is coherent, [lem-pc-coherent-hi] applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ gives that $H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. Hence $V$ is finite-dimensional and has a basis.

Hypothesis (0) says that the evaluation map from $V$ generates $\mathcal L$. Therefore the basis defines $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}:X\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ by [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], and the construction identifies $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}^*\mathcal O(1)$ with $\mathcal L$ using [def-pc-projective-space-twist].

The morphism $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}$ is proper: its composite with $\mathbf P(V^\vee)\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is the proper morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, and projective space is separated over $k$, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] applies.

Condition (1) makes $\varphi_{\mathcal L,V}$ injective on closed points: if $x\ne y$ had the same projective image, every section vanishing at $x$ would vanish at $y$, contradicting (1). The closed-fibre argument is the statement of [lem-sc-point-tangent-closed-fibre-singleton]: for every closed point $p$ the fibre is empty or exactly $\{x\}$, with $x$ closed. Its proof uses that a nonempty fibre is closed and therefore has a closed point by [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point], while any nonclosed point in a finite-type scheme has infinitely many closed specializations by [lem-sc-finite-type-nonclosed-closure-closed-points], contradicting injectivity. Hence every fibre over a closed point is finite.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, proof after condition (1), with Tags 005E and 0478 for the closed-point details

proof.text: Apply [thm-sc-proper-finite-fibre-finite-neighbourhood] (Tag 02OH) at each closed point $p$ of $\mathbf P(V^\vee)$, using properness from step 3, the finite closed fibre from step 4, and that $\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], being of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$. This gives an open neighbourhood $U_p$ on which $\varphi$ is finite. The union of the $U_p$ contains every closed point; its closed complement, if nonempty, would contain a closed point by [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point], since projective space is quasi-compact and Kolmogorov. Thus the union is all of $\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ and $\varphi$ is finite.

It remains to prove surjectivity of $\varphi^\sharp:\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V^\vee)}\to\varphi_*\mathcal O_X$. Since $\varphi$ is finite, $\varphi_*\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V^\vee)}$-module of finite type [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence so is the cokernel of $\varphi^\sharp$; its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed], and if nonempty it contains a closed point of $\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ by [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point]. So it suffices to check surjectivity on stalks at closed points $p$. If the fibre over $p$ is empty, then $p$ is not in the closed set $\varphi(X)$ and $(\varphi_*\mathcal O_X)_p=0$. For a closed $p$ with fibre $\{x\}$, the equality of sets from [lem-sc-point-tangent-closed-fibre-singleton] and the closedness of the proper map $\varphi$ (step 3) show that the $\varphi^{-1}(U)$, for $U$ running through the open neighbourhoods of $p$, form a fundamental system of open neighbourhoods of $x$; this identifies $(\varphi_*\mathcal O_X)_p$ with $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and the stalk map is finite because $\varphi$ is finite. Both residue fields are $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], since the source and projective target are of finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$.

Condition (2) says that $T_{X/k,x}\to T_{\mathbf P(V^\vee)/k,p}$ is injective. By [lem-sc-point-tangent-cotangent-surjective], the induced map $\mathfrak m_p/\mathfrak m_p^2\to\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$ is surjective.

The finite local stalk map has equal residue fields and is surjective on cotangent spaces, so [lem-sc-point-tangent-finite-local-cotangent-surjective] gives a surjection $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P,p}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Hence $\varphi^\sharp$ is surjective on all stalks (step 6), so on every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $\mathbf P(V^\vee)$, whose inverse image $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine because $\varphi$ is finite, the ring map $R\to A$ is surjective; thus $\varphi$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion].
When $V=H^0(X,\mathcal L)$, this is the complete linear system, and [def-sc-ample] identifies the closed-immersion property and pullback isomorphism with very ampleness.

lean.statement: theorem point_tangent_separation_closed_immersion (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (V : Submodule k ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).obj (L.val.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)))) (hgen : ∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → ∃ s : V, x ∈ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val) (hpoint : ∀ x y : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → IsClosed ({y} : Set X) → x ≠ y → ∃ s : V, x ∉ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val ∧ y ∈ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val) (htangent : ∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → ∀ θ : schemeTangentSpace k X f x, θ ≠ 0 → ∃ s : V, x ∉ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus L s.val ∧ ((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction θ.val)).unit.app L).val.app (Opposite.op ⊤) s.val ≠ 0) : FiniteDimensional k V ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) [Finite I] (b : Module.Basis I k V), ∃ s : I → L.sections, (∀ i, (s i).val (Opposite.op ⊤) = (b i).val) ∧ ∃ hs : Epi (L.freeHomEquiv.symm s), IsClosedImmersion (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections I f L s hs) ∧ Nonempty (ProjectiveSpace.twistRestrict (ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections I f L s hs) 1 ≅ L)) ∧ (V = ⊤ → IsVeryAmple f L)
